text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Merging state-owned bank Postipankki with state financing institution Vientiluotto would help bank's privatisation plans, says Anssi Rauramo, head of Postipankki supervisory board.
- Government convenes to discuss the budget proposal on Wednesday.
- In budget negotiations, Social Democrats want to agree on principles of tax relief for low-income workers and the retired. Final decision on possible tax break would come after pay talks.
- Construction sector overheating should not be exaggerated, the sector is actually in recession in many parts of the country, Leftist Alliance says.
- Current budget proposal model does not give enough information for parliament to use its power -- system should be reviewed, State Economy Comptroller's Office says.
- Salary gap between men and women has remained in Finland despite provisos guaranteeing equal pay, a study shows.
- Summer heatwave lifted sales of beer and soft drinks strongly, by 25 percent from summer 1996, sector says.
- Finns regaining courage to take apartment loans, new loans rose by one-fourth from first of half of last year.
- Statistics Finland tries to improve exactness of statistics used in country measurement according to EMU criteria.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Finnish top firms get international syndicated loans a lot cheaper than their European competitors; in small Finnish markets many international banks compete to offer cheap money, U.S. banker says.
- Possible merger between power grop IVO and oil group Neste would hike electricity prices, Industry Federation says.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Competitive cooperation with rival Nokia brings dynamism, Swedish telecoms group Ericsson's Finnish managing director Veli-Matti Mattila says.

- Additional budget cuts of even 17 billion markka would not be a catastrophe, Finland is clearly living in an economic boom, Matti Viren, director of reseach at the Government Institute of Economic Research (VATT) says.
- European Commission's budget and financial affairs commissioner Finnish Erkki Liikanen said to be possible successor to current chairman Jacques Santer.
- Finnish customs at Helsinki airport confiscated a record 50,000 pirate CDs on their way to Russia.
DEMARI
- Government's budget line implies wrong kind of saving, Christian League says.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
